arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import parse

# Test with actual parse results
print('=== Real parse examples ===')

# Example 1: fixed values
r = parse.parse('hello {}', 'hello world')
print('Result:', r)
print('world in r:', 'world' in r)
print('hello in r:', 'hello' in r)  # This shouldn't match since 'hello' isn't parsed

# Example 2: named values
r = parse.parse('Name: {name}', 'Name: Alice')
print('\nResult:', r)
print('name in r:', 'name' in r)
print('Alice in r:', 'Alice' in r)
print('bob in r:', 'bob' in r)

# Example 3: mixed
r = parse.parse('{} and {thing}', 'spam and eggs')
print('\nResult:', r)
print('spam in r:', 'spam' in r)
print('eggs in r:', 'eggs' in r)
print('thing in r:', 'thing' in r)
print('and in r:', 'and' in r)  # 'and' is not a parsed value

# Example 4: numeric types
r = parse.parse('Age: {:d}, Score: {:f}', 'Age: 25, Score: 99.5')
print('\nResult:', r)
print('25 in r:', 25 in r)
print('99.5 in r:', 99.5 in r)
print('age in r:', 'age' in r)
"
